correction: The first-day claim is too broad if it means a binding ceiling constrains every DiGA from its first reimbursed sale. Under the framework’s ordinary group rules, § 3d expressly exempts up to 2,000 redeemed codes per DiGA ID in the first year. This is not a universal exemption for every route: the fallback-group treatment differs. The GKV implementation page, last updated 5 October 2026 before this submission, repeats the initial exemption. The framework also contains defined category exceptions. A legal ceiling framework exists, but that does not establish an effective ceiling for every application from day one.
effect: This weakens the specific factual rebuttal used to call the GKV report misleading and to support manufacturer agreement over reporting definitions. It leaves the separate arguments about balanced reporting and practical data collection open.
limits: The strongest benign reading is shorthand for the applicability of the general framework and group assignment from listing, rather than a claim that every sale is immediately capped. The association correctly identifies a legally mandated, jointly negotiated framework. Nevertheless its universal first-day wording is used to rebut first-year pricing discretion without acknowledging the express initial exemption. This narrow issue does not establish that the GKV report is unbiased, that every manufacturer can charge any amount indefinitely, that a particular price was lawful or unlawful, or that the reporting proposal is unwise. No intent inferred.
context_and_alternatives: All 45 author pages were read. Physical page 16 was rendered and visually checked; pages 15–16 contain the complete request and justification. The association welcomes ending the annual report, challenges its tone and asks for shared determination of statistical parameters.

The actual 2025 GKV report, published 1 April 2026, uses unilateral-pricing language in its executive summary, but its complete ceiling section on physical pages 23–25 explicitly describes the framework, the initial exemption and other exceptions. Do not portray the entire report as denying the existence of ceilings, or treat the policy disagreement over its language as the error.
Framework group assignment can operate retrospectively from listing under § 3b(5), while § 3d separately exempts initial quantities. This is the concrete framework-versus-effective-cap alternative.

Current § 134(5) contains a mandatory fallback-group ceiling provision. It still makes ceilings dependent on utilisation. The pre-submission October 2026 implementation explanation explicitly retains the 2,000-code exemption. No conclusion about every old fallback-group clause remaining unchanged is needed.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the scope error concerns one specific rebuttal in a broader request about reporting governance. No aggregate price effect or patient impact is established. Materiality is independent of its direction.
direction_explanation: True narrowly: presenting universal immediate ceilings makes the GKV report’s pricing criticism appear less defensible and supports the author’s request for manufacturer agreement on reporting definitions. Correcting the exemption weakens that particular rationale.
